reasons: Failures when saving to the account are hidden from the visitor.
The code saves the language even for signed-out visitors, which the comment does not mention.

terms.meaning: a small piece of data the browser stores and sends back with each request
a function that is called whenever something it watches changes
asking the server to draw the current page again with fresh data

sections.name: File setup, listeners
sections.title: Shared listeners and imports
sections.what: Brings in the tools and sets up one shared list of components waiting for a language change.
sections.why: Likely reason: all language-aware pieces update together when the button is pressed.
sections.watch_out: The list lives only in this browser tab's memory, so other tabs do not hear about a change until they reload.

sections.name: readLang, subscribe
sections.title: Reading and subscribing to language
sections.what: Reads the language from the cookie. If the cookie is missing or holds an unknown value, English is used. Also lets a component register to receive change notices.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cookie is the single source of truth, and English is a safe fallback.
sections.watch_out: The cookie name is placed into a pattern, so the name must stay simple text.

sections.name: useLang
sections.title: Hook for the current language
sections.what: Gives a component the current language and keeps it updated. During server drawing, it returns English.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server has no cookie, so English is the safe starting value.
sections.watch_out: If the server and the browser disagree on the language, the text can flicker when the page loads.

sections.name: LangToggle
sections.title: The language button
sections.what: Shows a button labelled EN or with the Hindi letter. When pressed, it writes the cookie, notifies listeners, sends the choice to the server, and refreshes the page.
sections.why: The comment says it saves to the cookie and to the account when signed in.
sections.watch_out: The code sends the language to the server even when no one is signed in, while the comment says only signed-in visitors are saved. The server must handle that case.

summary: A button that switches the site between English and Hindi, stores the choice in a cookie, and saves it to the account when the visitor is signed in.
purpose: Lets a visitor change language on any page, and keeps every language-aware piece of the page in step.
why: The comment says the language lives in a cookie and components re-read it when the toggle changes it. The account save is described in the button's comment.
how: 1. Each component reads the current language from the cookie. 2. When the button is pressed, the next language is chosen, the cookie is written for one year, and all listening components are told to update. 3. The new language is sent to the server to save on the account. 4. The page data is refreshed.
inputs: The cookie named by LANG_COOKIE, and the button press.
outputs: An updated cookie, a request to /api/me/language, a refreshed page, and a button showing EN or the Hindi letter.
risks: If the account save fails, the failure is ignored, so the account may keep the old language while the cookie shows the new one.
debug: If the language does not change, check the cookie in browser storage and the language validity check. If the choice does not carry to other devices, check the /api/me/language route and its response.
